The three third-party stylesheets the MyST book theme loads, and why they are here
=================================================================================

Until 2026-10-16 every page of this site fetched three stylesheets from two CDNs:

    cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.15.2/dist/katex.min.css
    cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.css
    cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jupyter-matplotlib@0.11.3/css/mpl_widget.css

and, on any page with mathematics, up to twenty font files from jsdelivr on top -- nine
of them on expectation-variance alone, pulled by the KaTeX stylesheet relative to its own
URL.

All three are render-blocking, none of them could be preloaded (a stylesheet is
discovered before its own contents are), and all of them hand a third party the IP
address of every reader of a book that devotes a chapter to the GDPR. _site/fonts/ already
records that argument for the Google Fonts @import; this is the same argument for the rest
of the page. The two cases differ only in who had to be asked: the @import was ours to
delete, these are the theme's markup, so they are rewritten after the build instead.

Committed rather than fetched during the build, for the same reasons as the webfonts: a
deploy must not depend on a third party being up, and the bytes must not change
underneath us.


What is here, and that it is unmodified
---------------------------------------

**Nothing in this directory has been edited.** Every file is exactly what the CDN served,
which is the property that makes it checkable against upstream later. In particular the
stylesheets still reference `.woff`, `.ttf`, `.eot` and `.svg` variants that are
deliberately *not* vendored -- see the note at the end.

katex/katex.min.css
  23,112 bytes
  sha256 f7808d67f6c9b70ac1619ad7842381be9078ad9533067bc0b22ac5bf7d53306a
  from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.15.2/dist/katex.min.css
  sha384-MlJdn/WNKDGXveldHDdyRP1R4CTHr3FeuDNfhsLPYrq2t0UBkUdK2jyTnXPEK1NQ
  ^ this is the integrity hash the theme itself published on the <link> it
    emitted, so the vendored copy is provably the exact bytes the site was
    already loading. Verified at vendor time.

font-awesome/css/font-awesome.css
  37,414 bytes
  sha256 36e0a7e08bee65774168528938072c536437669c1b7458ac77976ec788e4439c
  from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.css

  911 bytes
  sha256 e14a545216f676853ee3ff11b2d906f06620f62c7f700a5092fa65ccb1016abb
  from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jupyter-matplotlib@0.11.3/css/mpl_widget.css

katex/fonts/*.woff2
  20 files, 259,792 bytes total
  from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.15.2/dist/fonts/<name>
  Every woff2 the stylesheet names. Which of the twenty a reader actually downloads
  depends on the mathematics on the page: nine on expectation-variance, none on a
  chapter without formulae.

font-awesome/fonts/fontawesome-webfont.woff2
  77,160 bytes
  sha256 2adefcbc041e7d18fcf2d417879dc5a09997aa64d675b7a3c4b6ce33da13f3fe
  from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/fonts/fontawesome-webfont.woff2

Licences
--------

    katex/LICENSE               MIT, Khan Academy and other contributors
    font-awesome/LICENSE        font SIL OFL 1.1, CSS MIT, Dave Gandy
    jupyter-matplotlib/LICENSE  BSD 3-clause, Matplotlib Contributors

All three permit redistribution. The OFL requires its licence to travel with the font,
which is what font-awesome/LICENSE is for.


Why Font Awesome is here at all, when nothing on the page uses it
-----------------------------------------------------------------

It looks unused and nearly is: across all thirty built pages there is **not one** element
with a `fa-` class, and the browser reports the FontAwesome face as `unloaded` on every
page -- the stylesheet is fetched and the font it asks for never is.

It is not unused. The theme's client bundle contains `"fa fa-"` together with `fa-play`,
`fa-stop`, `fa-pause`, `fa-check`, `fa-times`, `fa-caret` and `fa-retweet`: these are
thebe's run / stop / restart controls, which appear only once a reader makes a notebook
live. Deleting the stylesheet -- the obvious move on the evidence of a normal page load --
would have left those buttons as blank squares in the one feature that most needs them to
be legible.

So: vendored, not removed. On an ordinary page view this costs one same-origin stylesheet
and no font at all.


Why only the woff2, and nothing is edited
------------------------------------------

The stylesheets name four or five formats per face; only the woff2 is vendored. Every
browser that can run this site has supported woff2 since 2016, woff2 is listed before the
older formats in every one of these `src` lists, and _site/fonts/ already ships
woff2-only for the same reason.

The alternative was to strip the other formats out of the CSS, which would have left no
dangling references -- and would have meant these files were no longer byte-for-byte what
upstream published, so the sha256 above would check nothing. Keeping them exact and
accepting references that only a pre-2016 browser would follow is the better trade: a
reference nobody requests costs nothing, and verifiability is worth something.


Updating them
-------------

tools/vendor_assets.py fails the build if the theme starts asking for a version other than
the one vendored here, and names both versions when it does. That is the signal to refetch
all of it -- stylesheet, fonts and licence -- check the hashes, and update this file. It is
deliberately a failure and not a fallback to the CDN: silently going back to jsdelivr is
the exact outcome this directory exists to prevent.
